facts.statement: Hintighernia is a newly described genus and species of tapejarid pterosaur.
Hintighernia lived during the Cretaceous period.
Its fossils were found in the Cambridge Greensand of the United Kingdom.
Hintighernia’s fossil range is the Early Cretaceous.
Hintighernia is a tapejarid pterosaur from the Early Cretaceous Cambridge Greensand, United Kingdom.
facts.quote: Hintighernia is a genus of tapejarid pterosaur from the Early Cretaceous of the Cambridge Greensand, United Kingdom.

facts.statement: The type species of the genus is Hintighernia edingerae.
facts.quote: The type species is H. edingerae.

facts.statement: The genus name derives from a cranium that had previously been assigned to Ornithostoma.
facts.quote: It was named from a cranium originally referred to the genus Ornithostoma.

facts.statement: The partial cranium CAMSM B54406, formerly linked to Ornithostoma sedgwicki, is identified as a sinopterine tapejarid and assigned to Hintighernia edingerae.
Micro‑CT scanning shows that Hintighernia’s neuroanatomy closely resembles that of Tapejara wellnhoferi.
Additional Cambridge Greensand remains are also referred to Tapejaridae, and an isolated rostrum fragment is tentatively assigned to cf. Hintighernia.
Ornithostoma sedgwicki is considered a chaoyangopterid azhdarchoid with a hypodigm limited to four jaw fragments.
Researchers suggest that a third, non‑azhdarchid azhdarchoid species may also be present in the Cambridge Greensand.
Europe is proposed as an early hotspot of tapejarid phylogenetic diversity and a possible origin point for sinopterines and tapejarines.

rejected.statement: The genus was named by Pêgas et al. in 2026.
Diagnostic features include the shape of the upper temporal fenestra margins and a robust, elongate supraoccipital median ridge.
